doc.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Quincy Jones and the sessions for 'The Wiz'
summary: Raph tells of tuba and bass trombone sessions for 'The Wiz' and an overdub that ended with Quincy Jones kissing his cheek.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I wanted to mention a couple of people here that you’ve worked with. Quincy Jones?
I love Quincy. I love Quincy. He kissed me. Did I tell you that?

Yeah, right. We did, he did “The Wiz,” the movie “The Wiz,” which was huge sessions of many, many musicians. In fact on one session I played tuba along with Dave Bargeron, Don Butterfield and Tony Price. There were four tubas on this one particular session. And on another session I played bass trombone, and there were about six or eight trombones on the thing. And after the sessions were over I got a call from the contractor, could I come down to A&R and overdub something. So I came down. Tony Price was there. I came down on bass trombone. Tony was playing tuba. Both of us had to reinforce a bass line of one of the arrangements. It was about a three page, three trombone page arrangement. Sort of an uptempo and fairly busy. And we sat down and we played it and they took a balance and they recorded it. We played it twice. The second time was the take, and that was it. So we walked in to listen to it and Quincy’s listening to it, and he gets up and kisses me on the cheek, which meant see you later.
Yeah. I love Quincy. He deserves more than the success he’s got. I mean he’s the most successful person in the world and he deserves that plus.
